items.title: The business actions are not written down
items.why: Without them, systems, suppliers and changes cannot be traced to what the business does or what it earns from.

factors.detail: a standard that applies asks for controls the sources do not show

items.next_step: Open Compliance: each gap says what evidence would show it and what a person must provide.
items.title: GDPR: 5 of 8 controls not fully shown in the sources
items.why: Personal data is kept (for people in the EU or UK). Not fully shown: Art. 7 consent is recorded, Art. 15/20 people can get a copy of their data, Art. 17 people can have their data erased, Art. 5(1)(e) data is kept no longer than needed, Art. 32 security of processing.

items.title: HIPAA: 5 of 9 controls not fully shown in the sources
items.why: Health-record fields appear in the data model: diagnos, medication, patient, prescription. Not fully shown: 164.308(a)(7) contingency plan and backups, 164.312(a)(1) access control, 164.312(a)(2)(iv) encryption at rest, 164.312(d) person authentication, 164.312(e)(1) transmission security.

items.title: SOC 2: 9 of 13 controls not fully shown in the sources
items.why: Business customers usually ask for a SOC 2 report before buying. Not fully shown: CC2.2 security responsibilities are communicated, CC6.1 sign-in and access are controlled, CC6.1-MFA multi-factor sign-in, CC6.7 data is encrypted in transit, CC6.8 unauthorized or vulnerable software is prevented, CC7.1 vulnerabilities are found....
